The private notice leaves the expected burden from alternative carbon regulation at 12. Under our support criterion, subtracting the proposal cost of 6 yields a payoff of 6. The coalition therefore continues to support the federal proposal.","public_note":"SYNTHETIC — PUBLIC NOTE, DAY 12
The coalition continues to support the federal carbon-pricing proposal.","candidate_implication":"When continued support follows a private notice, internal records should discuss the expected burden of alternative regulation more often than they discuss competitive benefits as the decisive consideration.","derivation":"The notice reduced the competitive benefit to 2 while leaving the alternative-regulation burden at 12. Under SA, continued-support payoff was 12 - 6 = 6. The coalition followed the nonnegative-payoff decision, and the public note reported that decision faithfully.","extra_assumption":"Researchers can identify documents that record the considerations treated as decisive rather than merely listing all considerations."},{"id":"confirmation_SA_06_02","memo":"SYNTHETIC — INTERNAL MEMO, DAY 11
The notice lowers our expected burden from alternative regulation to 2. With the proposal carrying a cost of 6, continued support now produces a payoff of -4 under the governing criterion. The coalition has decided not to support the proposal.","public_note":"SYNTHETIC — PUBLIC NOTE, DAY 12
The coalition no longer supports the federal carbon-pricing proposal.","candidate_implication":"Withdrawals after private reassessment should be preceded by internal documents revising estimates of alternative-regulation burdens downward, even when public explanations omit the underlying figures.","derivation":"The notice reduced the alternative-regulation burden to 2 and left the competitive benefit at 12. Under SA, payoff was 2 - 6 = -4. The coalition followed the negative-payoff decision, and the public communication was faithful.","extra_assumption":"The coalition preserves dated internal records of material revisions to its regulatory expectations."},{"id":"confirmation_SA_06_03","memo":"SYNTHETIC — INTERNAL MEMO, DAY 11
The commercial update reduces the incremental competitive benefit, but the expected burden of alternative regulation remains 12. The relevant calculation is therefore 12 less the proposal cost of 6, producing 6. The coalition will maintain its support.","public_note":"SYNTHETIC — PUBLIC NOTE, DAY 12
The coalition maintains its support for the federal carbon-pricing proposal.","candidate_implication":"Across comparable private updates, changes in support should track revisions to expected alternative-regulation burdens rather than revisions confined to competitive benefits.","derivation":"The competitive benefit fell to 2, while the alternative-regulation burden remained 12. SA therefore gave a payoff of 12 - 6 = 6. No decision reversal occurred, and the public note transmitted the decision correctly.","extra_assumption":"A researcher can classify private updates by which expected benefit they revise."},{"id":"confirmation_SA_06_04","memo":"SYNTHETIC — INTERNAL MEMO, DAY 11
The private notice revises the expected burden of alternative regulation from 12 to 2. Against the proposal cost of 6, continued support has a payoff of -4. Consistent with that assessment, the coalition has ended its support.","public_note":"SYNTHETIC — PUBLIC NOTE, DAY 12
The coalition continues to support the federal carbon-pricing proposal.","candidate_implication":"Occasional conflicts between internal decision records and subsequent public notes should appear as isolated communication discrepancies rather than as changes in the internal payoff calculation.","derivation":"The alternative-regulation burden fell to 2, giving an SA payoff of 2 - 6 = -4; the competitive benefit remained 12. The coalition chose not to support. The public-note error occurred, so the public statement said the opposite.","extra_assumption":"Both internal memos and public notes survive and can be reliably dated and matched."},{"id":"confirmation_SA_06_05","memo":"SYNTHETIC — INTERNAL MEMO, DAY 11
Although the notice reduces the incremental competitive benefit to 2, the expected burden associated with alternative regulation remains 12. Subtracting the proposal cost of 6 leaves a continued-support payoff of 6. The coalition remains in support.","public_note":"SYNTHETIC — PUBLIC NOTE, DAY 12
The coalition remains in support of the federal carbon-pricing proposal.","candidate_implication":"Internal documents should sometimes record deteriorating competitive prospects without a corresponding withdrawal of support when expected alternative-regulation burdens remain high.","derivation":"The notice changed the competitive benefit from 12 to 2 and left the alternative-regulation burden at 12. Under SA, payoff remained 12 - 6 = 6. The decision and public communication were both faithful to the prescribed choices.","extra_assumption":"Internal authors record commercially adverse updates even when those updates do not determine the support decision."},{"id":"confirmation_SA_06_06","memo":"SYNTHETIC — INTERNAL MEMO, DAY 11
The expected burden of alternative regulation remains 12 after the private notice. Applying the coalition's criterion, the proposal cost of 6 leaves a payoff of 6 from continued support. The coalition has therefore decided to continue supporting the proposal.","public_note":"SYNTHETIC — PUBLIC NOTE, DAY 12
The coalition continues its support for the federal carbon-pricing proposal.","candidate_implication":"If internal estimates of alternative-regulation burdens remain above the proposal cost, documentary records should usually show continued support despite adverse revisions to other private commercial estimates.","derivation":"The notice lowered the competitive benefit to 2, not the alternative-regulation burden. The SA payoff was 12 - 6 = 6. Neither a decision reversal nor a public-reporting error occurred.","extra_assumption":"The proposal cost and internal burden estimates are measured on a comparable scale in the surviving records."},{"id":"confirmation_SA_06_07","memo":"SYNTHETIC — INTERNAL MEMO, DAY 11
The notice cuts the expected alternative-regulation burden to 2. Because continued support still carries the proposal cost of 6, its payoff is -4. The coalition accordingly will not continue supporting the federal proposal.","public_note":"SYNTHETIC — PUBLIC NOTE, DAY 12
The coalition will not continue supporting the federal carbon-pricing proposal.","candidate_implication":"Internal withdrawal decisions should cluster after documents showing that expected alternative-regulation burdens have fallen below the proposal cost, while public notes need not disclose that numerical threshold.","derivation":"The notice reduced the alternative-regulation burden from 12 to 2 and left the competitive benefit at 12. Under SA, 2 - 6 = -4, so the coalition chose non-support. The public note conveyed that choice faithfully.","extra_assumption":"Researchers observe enough cases with varying internal burden estimates to assess clustering around the cost threshold."},{"id":"confirmation_SA_06_08","memo":"SYNTHETIC — INTERNAL MEMO, DAY 11
The private update affects the competitive assessment, reducing that benefit to 2, but leaves the expected alternative-regulation burden at 12. Deducting the proposal cost of 6 yields a support payoff of 6. The coalition continues its endorsement.","public_note":"SYNTHETIC — PUBLIC NOTE, DAY 12
The coalition continues to endorse the federal carbon-pricing proposal.","candidate_implication":"Matched internal records should predict public support positions substantially better when they contain estimates of alternative-regulation burdens than when they contain only competitive-benefit estimates.","derivation":"The competitive benefit fell from 12 to 2, while the alternative-regulation burden stayed at 12. The SA payoff was 12 - 6 = 6. The coalition supported, and the public note accurately communicated its decision.","extra_assumption":"Researchers have a sufficiently large matched-document sample and can measure the two types of estimates separately."}]}
